Man, being stable in this way, due to their (God's) omnipotence, should serve the Supreme Soul situated in their heart. Because they are omnipotent, God is eternal and
infinite, therefore they are the ultimate goal of life, and by worshiping them, man can remove the cause of bound life. Meaning: As is made clear by the Bhagavad-gita (18.61), Lord Krishna is the all-pervading Supreme Being.
Therefore, the Yogi can only worship them, because they are not an illusion, but
a fact that every living being is engaged in some service. The natural state of living beings is to serve
them, but in the illusionary environment or in the bondage of existence, the bound soul thinks of serving only illusion. The bound soul engages in serving his perishable body, his physical relatives like wife and children, and
the body and the relationships of the body, such as home, land, property, society, and country, which are necessary
for serving the necessities, But he doesn't know that all this service
is completely misleading. Before this, we have told many times that this physical world is itself an illusion--
Like a mirage in the desert. In the desert, there is an illusion of water, and foolish animals, becoming victims of such illusion, run in the desert for water, although there is not even a trace of water there.
But since there is no water in the desert, therefore no one draws the conclusion that there is water anywhere there. A wise man knows that water exists, but it is in the oceans, but such vast
water bodies are very far from the desert. Therefore, man should seek water near the sea,
not in the desert. Each of us is engaged in the search for the real happiness of life, that is, eternal life, eternal
or infinite knowledge, and immortal blissful life. But the foolish person who
does not have knowledge of reality, he searches for the truth of life in illusion. This physical body is never eternal.

gradually becomes separated from his mother, although the mother keeps wanting the child to do some service.

is there. Similarly, since we are part of God, God always remains affectionate towards us and wants
to remain that we go back to His abode. But we are such bound souls that we do not care about them, and
